args.query: exchange-api 503 connect timeout upstream external provider

events.statement: order-service error_rate jumped from a ~0.2% baseline to 26.73% at the 11:00-11:15 bucket and stayed ~31% (still 30.99 at 12:45).
All 174 order-service ERROR entries in 10:30-12:00 match one pattern: 'exchange-gateway call failed: <n> Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)' (504).

exchange-gateway logs show 'upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder' first seen 11:01:25, plus 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable' and a circuit breaker opening at 11:03:26.
exchange-gateway upstream_latency_ms rose from ~118ms baseline to 8550.82ms at the 11:00 bucket and remained ~9200-9300ms through 12:45.
order-service latency_p99_ms rose from ~150ms to ~5300ms at the 11:00 bucket and stayed elevated (5301.2 at 12:45), consistent with the 5000ms upstream timeout.

exchange-gateway request_rate stayed flat (~270-279 req/s) and cpu_pct flat (~30%) across the window; order-service cpu_pct (~40%), memory_pct (~60%) and db_pool_in_use (~14 conns) were flat, and restarts stayed 0.
order-service v2.15.2 (summary 'Add idempotency keys to order submit') deployed 10:48 and rolled back at 11:16, but error_rate remained ~31% after rollback.
No order-service logs matched 'idempot' in 10:40-11:20, and no exchange-gateway deployments exist in 06:00-12:59.
search_historical_incidents returned HIST-103 'Order failures during exchange partner outage' with root_cause 'External exchange API outage on the partner side', category dependency_failure.
exchange-gateway was still logging upstream connect timeouts to api.exchange-partner.example at 12:58, i.e. the incident was ongoing at latest data.
The fault originates at the external exchange provider (exchange-api); exchange-gateway and order-service are downstream victims propagating the partner's timeouts/503s.
